To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the lowest energy configurations of the benzene-acetyylene and 1,3-trifluorbenzene-acetylene involve C-H...π interactions, (2) the lowest energy configuration of the coronene-acetylne complex involves both π–π and C-H...π interaction, and (3) the C–H stretching vibrational frequency of acetylene is red-shifted in all of the complexes studied here.

the lowest energy structure is characterized by acetylene located over to the center of aromatic ring for benzene-acetylne complex, while the lowest-energy configuration for 1.3.5-trifluoro-benzene-acetyne complex is characterized by C-H...F hydrogen bond and C-H...π interaction, and the lowest energy structure of the coronene-acetylne complexes involves both π- π and C-H... π interactions.
the C−F…π interaction is stronger than C−H… π interaction, and the strength of C–H…π interaction depends upon the number of π-clouds available for C−H… interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the C−H… π interaction of benzene, fluorobenzene and acetylenes.
the C−H… π interactions of acetylenes with benzene, fluorinated-benzene, and coronene.
the strength of the C− H...π interactions in the acetylene-aromatic complexes and the effect of the C−F bonds of the 1,3-trifluorbenzene on the C− H..π interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C−F...π interaction is not as strong as C−H...pi interaction, but it is not a weak interaction.
the binding strength of the C−F...π and π...π interactions are stronger than C−H... π interaction, while the C−H...π interaction is stronger than C−C...π and C−F...C interactions.
the strength of C-H...π interactions is not only dependent on the nature of the π-cloud of the aromatic ring, but also on the presence of the other interactions in the complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the C−F bond is more attractive than the C−H bond to interact with acetylene.
the binding strength of a complex depends on the nature of the interaction, i.e., C−H...X (X = π, F, π) and the strength of the interaction is in the order: C−H...
the binding strength of C− H…π interactions depends on the strength of the C− H bond and the nature of the substituent group(s) in the aromatic rings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the C− H…π interaction complex where C–H bond of benzene interacts with the π cloud of acetylene is the lowest energy complex, while the lowest-energy structure of 1,3-trifluorbenzene-acetylene possesses both C–H…π interaction and C–H…F hydrogen bond.
the C− H…π interaction is a strong noncovalent interaction that is not always weaker than the C−H…O interaction.
the C−C stretching frequency of the acetylene molecule is not sensitive to its interaction with benzene, coronene or 1,3.5-trifluoro-benzene.
